title: module-interface-refactor-playbook-practical
body:
Purpose
This doc is a practical playbook for refactoring our Terraform primitive modules (VPC, IAM, and K8s cluster primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS). Goal: produce stable module interfaces that are easier to upgrade, test, and adopt in private (VPC/on-prem) deployments without breaking customer stacks.

Scope
- Surface/interface design for primitive modules: vpc-network, iam-role, k8s-cluster (eks/gke/aks variants).
- Variable and output contract recommendations, semantic versioning rules, and migration recipes.
- CI/testing checklist and on-prem considerations (air-gapped, private registries).
- Rollout/canary and rollback guidance for infra teams.

Principles (short)
- Backward compatibility first: nonbreaking defaults; prefer additive changes.
- Explicit extension points: allow consumers to opt into new behavior via flags rather than implicit changes.
- Small surface area: keep module public API minimal.
- Observable migrations: migration steps produce auditable changes and have automated tests.

High-level module surface suggestions
1) vpc-network (primitive)
- Purpose: encapsulate network topology, subnets, route tables, NATs, and peering.
- Required variables (examples):
  - name_prefix (string)
  - cidr_block (string)
  - private_subnet_cidrs (list(string))
  - public_subnet_cidrs (list(string))
  - azs (list(string))
- Optional variables:
  - enable_nat_gateway (bool) default false
  - tags (map(string)) default {}
- Outputs to lock:
  - vpc_id (string)
  - private_subnet_ids (list(string))
  - public_subnet_ids (list(string))
  - route_table_ids (list(string))
- Compatibility notes: never rename vpc_id output; add new outputs with new names. Deprecate via shim outputs for one release cycle.

2) iam-role (primitive)
- Purpose: create least-privilege role templates for workloads; support assume-role by service accounts when using OIDC.
- Required variables:
  - role_name (string)
  - assumed_by (string) e.g. "ec2.amazonaws.com" or "eks.amazonaws.com"
- Optional:
  - inline_policies (map(string))
  - managed_policy_arns (list(string))
- Outputs:
  - role_arn (string)
  - role_id (string)

3) k8s-cluster primitive (cluster-agnostic api with provider-specific adapters)
- Design pattern: keep a minimal cluster module with a provider adapter pattern. Top-level module exposes generic variables. Provider adapters (eks/gke/aks) live in subfolders and implement provider-specific plumbing.
- Generic variables:
  - cluster_name
  - version
  - node_pool_definitions (list(object)) serialized as json string for simplicity in TF v0.12 consumers
  - network_subnet_ids (list(string))
  - control_plane_endpoint (optional) for private/onprem clusters
- Outputs that must be stable:
  - kubeconfig_content (string) or kubeconfig_path
  - cluster_endpoint
  - cluster_ca_cert
  - node_pool_ids

Variable and output naming conventions (practical rules)
- use snake_case, short names, consistent pluralization (e.g., _ids for lists).
- Prefer explicit type hints in README and examples (even if TF doesn't enforce type).
- Avoid using provider-prefixed names in top-level primitives (no aws_vpc_id in generic vpc module). Use neutral names (vpc_id).
- Add duck-typed compatibility outputs when renaming: keep old output name and mark deprecated in README for at least one major release.

Versioning and compatibility policy
- Follow SemVer for modules: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
- Breaking changes require MAJOR bump and a migration guide. Minor releases add features/backwards-compatible additions. Patch releases fix bugs.
- Deprecation window: keep deprecated outputs/variables for at least one MINOR release, with clear warnings in plan/apply logs (via null_resource local-exec that warn?).

Upgrade/migration recipes (common patterns)
1) Nonbreaking addition (e.g., add new optional var or output)
- Bump MINOR, publish. Consumers can opt-in by setting the var. No state changes expected.

2) Rename Output (breaking) - safe migration pattern
- Add new output name while keeping old output with same value (shim).
- Bump MINOR and mark old output deprecated in README.
- After one MINOR cycle (and consumer adoption), remove old output in MAJOR.
- If state needs to move (resource address renaming), provide explicit terraform state mv commands and a script. Example: "terraform state mv module.old.module.vpc.aws_vpc.main module.new.module.vpc.aws_vpc.main".

3) Resource shape change that alters IDs (e.g., switching from launch_config to launch_template)
- Implement dual-resource strategy: create new resource with new name, output both ids, and keep old resource until consumers migrate.
- Provide an automated migration plan in a test harness.

State migration checklist (must-run before MAJOR removal)
- Write and validate terraform state mv commands in a staging workspace.
- Produce a changelog with exact commands for customers.
- Run migration on a small canary customer stack (internal account) and verify resources unchanged post-migration.
- Have rollback steps (state backup and restore instructions).

CI and test harness
- Per-module acceptance tests (in GH actions):
  - plan-only checks against multiple TF versions (1.1, 1.3, 1.5 LTS we support)
  - apply/destroy in ephemeral accounts (short-lived) for smoke tests
  - static checks: tflint, tfsec with tailored rule set for private deployments (e.g., ensure no public S3 by default)
  - unit-like tests: generate sample var sets and validate outputs presence and types using terratest or kitchen-terraform.
- Add a compatibility matrix file in module repo root that lists which TF versions and provider versions are supported.

Canary and rollout strategy for module changes
- Internal canary first: pick 2 internal stacks (one hosted, one private on-prem staging) to run the new module.
- Customer beta: invite 3–5 customers to opt-in to the new module (via feature flag in our internal modules registry).
- Full rollout after 2 successful weeks with no regression alerts.
- Metrics to observe during canary: plan diffs, apply failures, resource churn, downtime incidents, and infra-cost delta.

Rollback patterns
- Prefer non-destructive rollbacks: revert to previous module version and re-run plan/apply.
- If state was modified via terraform state mv, keep a state snapshot named with timestamp and module-version to restore.
- Document a fast manual rollback: exact terraform init/plan/apply steps plus state restore commands.

On-prem / air-gapped considerations
- Module distribution: publish tarball artifacts to an internal registry (module-archive/vX.Y.tar.gz). Provide checksums and signed manifests.
- Docker/provider providers: use an internal provider proxy or vendor binaries in air-gapped bundles.
- Kubeconfig and CA handling: do not assume metadata services. Provide explicit variables for control plane endpoints and CA bundles.
- Private container registries: allow node pool to reference image_registry variable.

Provider-specific quirks (short notes)
- EKS: recommend using IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) via OIDC. Provide an optional var enable_irsa.
- GKE: ensure workload identity settings are explict; expose project-level bindings in readme.
- AKS: managed identity naming collisions can occur across subscriptions; recommend cluster-scoped unique prefixes.

Operational runbook snippets (for infra team)
- Pre-upgrade checklist: review open PRs, run tflint/tfsec, snapshot remote state, notify stakeholders.
- During upgrade: run terraform plan with -out, inspect for unexpected delete/create, run apply if plan is safe.
- Post-upgrade: run smoke tests (kube ping, service list), reconcile tags and monitoring annotations.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide if we adopt a single top-level "primitive-registry" repo or keep modules per team. Pros/cons doc needed (Jared to draft).
- How to emit deprecation warnings programmatically in TF plan? (tf doesn't support warnings; look at pre-apply scripts)
- Standardize node_pool_definitions schema (Sofia to propose JSON schema).

Quick example (README-style snippet)
- Example minimal usage of vpc-network:
  module "core_vpc" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//vpc-network?ref=v1.4.0"
    name_prefix = "redwood-stg"
    cidr_block = "10.10.0.0/16"
    private_subnet_cidrs = ["10.10.1.0/24","10.10.2.0/24"]
    public_subnet_cidrs = ["10.10.3.0/24"]
    azs = ["us-west-2a","us-west-2b"]
  }

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive: aim for a safe upgrade path rather than idealized purity.
- We should validate the migration recipes in a sprint and capture exact state mv commands as a follow-up.

Unresolved: exact deprecation cadence (minor vs major) for modules used by external customers.

Action items
- Jared: draft module registry pros/cons doc (due 2026-01-05).
- Sofia: propose JSON schema for node_pool_definitions (due 2026-01-12).
- Ben: set up GH actions acceptance pipeline (proof-of-concept) and run against vpc-network module (due 2026-01-20).

End of playbook draft.
